lede: The web split its attention on Monday, October 12, with no single story taking over. The clearest cross-feed signal was tennis: Felix Auger-Aliassime trended on Google search at the same time Polymarket ran a live market on his Shanghai Rolex Masters match. The biggest raw numbers sat elsewhere, with Counter-Strike 2 holding more than 1.4 million concurrent players on Steam and Wikipedia's most-read page, Money in the Bank (2026), drawing about 249,000 views in a near dead heat with Mathematics just behind it.

throughlines.title: felix auger aliassime
throughlines.gist: Auger-Aliassime trended on Google search while Polymarket ran a live betting market on his Shanghai Rolex Masters match against Pablo Carreno Busta.

throughlines.title: san antonio
throughlines.gist: A coincidence of names: a fatal highway crash in San Antonio, Texas trended on Google while USGS logged an earthquake near San Antonio de los Cobres, Argentina.

throughlines.title: Money in the Bank (2026)
throughlines.gist: The WWE event was Wikipedia's most-read article at about 249,000 views, narrowly ahead of Mathematics and List of equations.
